en: Vimānavatthu:
Purisavimāna,
Mahārathavagga
10. The First Nāga-Vimāna Story Having mounted the very white-naveled nāga,
the tusked one, free from dust, powerful, and of great speed;
Having mounted a well-prepared, excellent elephant,
he came here through the air across the sky.
He was fashioned upon the two tusks of the elephant.
The lotus ponds with their clear waters are in full bloom;
amidst the lotuses, throngs of musical instruments resound,
and these enchanting nymphs dance.
You have attained divine power and possess great majesty;
while still a human being, what merit did you perform?
By what means has your majesty become so radiant?
"And your radiance illuminates all directions.
That son of the gods, being questioned by Moggallāna, was filled with joy.
When asked the question,
he explained the fruit of that action:
"Only eight jasmine flowers..."
In the stupa of Kassapa, the Great Seer,
I offered [flowers] with my own hands, full of faith.
"Because of that, my complexion is such as this...
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The first Nāga-vimāna, the tenth.
